summary: Read-only audit of three untouched game areas, each finding adversarially verified against the code

confirmed.title: Holding E at the Peddler opens the stall, then shuts it about half a second later
confirmed.steps: Walk up to the Peddler so the plate reads THE PEDDLER [E] DEAL. Press and hold E, the way the game trains you to for every crate search and for HOLD E TO EXTRACT. On the first frame, updatePlayer opens the stall. After the OS key-repeat delay (about 0.5 s with Windows defaults), the browser sends keydown E with repeat=true. The window listener passes it to raidKey(e.code,e.repeat,e). The stall block has no !repeat test, so it sets G.trade=null and G.pedLock=1. Because E is still down, pedLock keeps the stall from reopening. The player sees the panel flash open and vanish with nothing said, and has to let go and tap E again. Every other one-press toggle in raidKey ignores key repeats (v15.49). The controller is not affected because pad X only sends fresh presses.
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, stand the player 50 units from the Peddler with no container within 46 units and clear keys. Dispatch a window keydown {code:'KeyE'} and step one updatePlayer frame, then assert G.trade is the Peddler. Next, dispatch a window keydown {code:'KeyE', repeat:true} and assert G.trade is still set. The current build sets it to null, so this fails. Control: send keyup E, then a fresh keydown {code:'KeyE', repeat:false}. G.trade must become null on both builds, which shows walking away with a fresh press still works. A fresh Escape must also still close the stall.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every step checks out in the current code.

1. The main window keydown listener has no general repeat filter for E. The only repeat guards before the hand-off are Backquote, Backspace, Tab (backOut) and the floor branch. The raid path ends in `raidKey(e.code,e.repeat,e);`.
2. None of the other keydown listeners touch E. The capture listener at ~12281 returns unless the key is Escape or Tab. The listeners at ~32079 and ~34235 are Escape/Tab only, and ~32218 needs INVHOVER on the hub or stage screen. So a repeated E reaches raidKey with repeat=true.
3. In raidKey, the open-stall block is `if(G&&!G.over&&G.trade){ ... if(code==='Escape'||code==='KeyE'||code==='Tab'||code==='KeyI'||code==='KeyB'){ G.trade=null; G.pedLock=1; return; }`. It has no `!repeat` test. The Digit line right below it does have one: `if(code.indexOf('Digit')===0&&!repeat){`.
4. updatePlayer opens the stall on the held key: `if(ped&&!crateUnderfoot&&!G.trade&&keys['KeyE']&&!G.pedLock){ G.pedLock=1; ... else { G.trade=ped; mouse.down=false; blip('pick'); } }`. It clears the lock only on release: `if(!keys['KeyE']) G.pedLock=0;`.
5. The only thing that sets `keys['KeyE']` false is the keyup listener, `window.addEventListener('keyup',function(e){ keys[e.code]=false; ...`. The pad X line also clears it, but only for the pad.

So when E is held, the first frame opens the stall. The first OS auto-repeat keydown (about 0.5 s later) runs the block above and closes it, and pedLock stays 1 until E is let go, so the stall does not reopen. No message is shown. No nearby comment says this is deliberate. The v8.28 comment is about pedOpen refusals, and the v15.49 comments say held keys should not flicker windows.

The pad is not affected. Pad X calls `raidKey('KeyE',false,null)` only on a fresh press (`pressed(2)&&!PAD.prev[2]`).

The proposed fix is correct. A repeat with the stall open now returns with no effect, which also stops it reaching the code below. A fresh E, ESC, I or B still closes the stall and sets pedLock. A fresh Tab is already handled earlier by backOut, and a repeat Tab is now a no-op. This is a bug fix, not a balance change, and it changes no player text.

confirmed.title: M opens the sector map over the open stall, then ESC, TAB and the number keys act on the hidden stall
confirmed.where: raidKey M toggle (~line 11080) and updatePlayer stall open (~line 16340)
confirmed.code:
if(code==='KeyM'&&G&&!G.over&&!repeat){ G.mapOpen=!G.mapOpen; }
    else { G.trade=ped; mouse.down=false; blip('pick'); }
confirmed.steps: Open the stall with E, then press M. The M toggle runs before the stall block, so the map opens. drawMapOverlay is drawn last and fills the screen at .94 opacity, so the stall is hidden behind it. Pressing E with the map already up gives the same result, because nothing in updatePlayer checks mapOpen. Now press ESC to close the map. The stall block handles ESC before the v12.89 map line, so the invisible stall closes and the map stays up. TAB goes through backOut, which checks G.trade before G.mapOpen, so it also closes the stall first. Worse, with the map up, the digits still belong to the stall: pressing 1 sells the whole backpack at the stall rate without the player seeing the panel. On a controller, the stall branch owns D-UP, so the map can never open over the stall there.
confirmed.fix:
if(code==='KeyM'&&G&&!G.over&&!G.trade&&!repeat){ G.mapOpen=!G.mapOpen; }
    else { G.trade=ped; G.mapOpen=false; mouse.down=false; blip('pick'); }
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, open the stall on the play path: stand at the Peddler, set keys E, and step a frame. Call raidKey('KeyM',false,null) and assert G.mapOpen===false. The current build gives true, so this fails. Second arm: set G.mapOpen=true with the stall closed, set keys E next to the Peddler, and step a frame. Assert that G.trade is set and G.mapOpen is false. The current build leaves the map open. Control: with G.trade null, raidKey('KeyM',false,null) must set G.mapOpen true on both builds, which proves the key path is live.

verdict.reason:
I checked every step against the current code and each one holds.

1. In raidKey, the M toggle comes before the stall block and has no stall guard: `if(code==='KeyM'&&G&&!G.over&&!repeat){ G.mapOpen=!G.mapOpen; }`. The stall block that follows (`if(G&&!G.over&&G.trade){`) only handles Escape/E/Tab/I/B, the digits, and G/Space/Q/C, so M goes straight through and opens the map over the stall.
2. In updatePlayer, the stall opens with `else { G.trade=ped; mouse.down=false; blip('pick'); }`. Nothing in updatePlayer reads mapOpen; the only mapOpen lines in that area are the downed reset. So pressing E with the map already up opens the stall underneath it. On a controller, pad X becomes KeyE through padHold even while the map is open, so the same thing happens there.
3. The draw order hides the stall: `if(G.trade) drawTrade();` comes first and `if(G.mapOpen) drawMapOverlay();` is drawn last. drawMapOverlay starts with `ctx.fillStyle='rgba(9,12,34,.94)'; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H);`, which covers the whole screen.
4. ESC closes the wrong thing. `if(code==='Escape'||code==='KeyE'||code==='Tab'||code==='KeyI'||code==='KeyB'){ G.trade=null; G.pedLock=1; return; }` runs before the v12.89 line that closes the map first, so the hidden stall closes and the map stays up. TAB goes through the document-level `if(backOut())`, and backOut checks `if(G.trade){...}` before `if(G.mapOpen){...}`, so TAB also closes the stall first.
5. The digits act on the hidden stall. `if(td===1) pedSellAll(); else if(td>=2&&td<=9) pedBuy(td-2);`, and pedSellAll sells every eligible backpack item at pedBuyRate the moment the key is pressed.
6. On a controller, the stall branch returns before the D-UP toggle `if(pressed(12)&&!bagNav&&!PAD.prev[12]&&G&&!G.over) G.mapOpen=!G.mapOpen;`, and inside that branch D-UP moves the row marker instead. So the pad cannot open the map over the stall; the only way it gets there is the map opening first, as in step 2.

Nothing marks this as deliberate. No comment or ruling says the map may sit over the stall. The v15.35 note "The map above still comes first" only describes the order of the mouse click handlers. It is not balance: no number or seeded draw is involved, and the fix changes no player text.

The proposed fix is correct and complete:
- Guarding M with !G.trade makes M do nothing while the stall is open, which matches "the open stall owns" the keys.
- Adding G.mapOpen=false to the stall-open line closes the map whenever the stall opens, including when pad X opens it.
- Those are the only two places that set mapOpen=true (line ~11080 and the pad D-UP), and D-UP cannot run while the stall is open. So no remaining path puts the map over the stall.

confirmed.title: Net lifetime earnings leave out stall money that was carried out
confirmed.where: runEarnings (~line 19948), called from addProgress via commitRun
confirmed.steps: In a raid, sell a backpack of found loot at the stall, for example to put $5,500 on G.pedCarry, then extract. endRaid pays P.credits+=G.pedCarry and the outcome card says 'Stall money carried out: $5,500, banked.' However, runEarnings counts only the items still in the backpack minus what the lift carried in. The Mainframe card 'Net lifetime earnings' ('everything you have extracted, minus everything you carried in') goes up by $0 for that run. If the player sold kit he carried up, the card goes down by the full carried-in value, even though he walked out with the money. The run row already stores the figure: rec.pedSold equals G.pedCarry, because pedSellAll is the only writer of either and adds the same amount to both.
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, runEarnings({outcome:'extract',haul:0,carriedIn:0,pedSold:5500}) must return 5500. The current build returns 0. On the real path: stage a backpack, call pedSellAll at the Peddler, endRaid('extract'), then commitRun(pendingRun). Assert that the P.netEarn delta equals haul-carriedIn+G.pedCarry, the same G.pedCarry that raised P.credits. Controls that must match on both builds: runEarnings({outcome:'dead',haul:0,carriedIn:0,pedSold:5500})===0, because stall money dies with you, and runEarnings({outcome:'extract',haul:4000,carriedIn:1000})===3000.

verdict.reason:
I checked every step against the current code and could not refute any of them.
(1) `function runEarnings(rec){ return ((rec.outcome==='extract')?(rec.haul||0):0)-(rec.carriedIn||0); }` exists as quoted. Its only callers are `netEarnFromLog` and `P.netEarn=(P.netEarn||0)+runEarnings(rec);` in `addProgress`, which `commitRun(pendingRun)` calls.
(2) `haul` is only the backpack at the end. In endRaid, `var T=G.tel,haul=0,i; for(i=0;i<G.bag.length;i++) haul+=ival(G.bag[i]);` runs after pedSellAll has already done `G.bag=kept;`, so anything sold at the stall is no longer in `haul`.
(3) The stall money is paid out on extraction: `if(G.pedCarry&&!G.sim){ P.credits+=G.pedCarry; }`. The outcome card then prints 'Stall money carried out: ... banked.'
(4) `rec.pedSold` equals `G.pedCarry`. The only writers of either value are `G.pedCarry=(G.pedCarry||0)+tot; G.pedSold=(G.pedSold||0)+tot; if(G.tel) G.tel.pedSold=G.pedSold;`. G and G.tel are built fresh for each raid, and the run record takes `pedSold:T.pedSold||0`.
(5) The card promises something the code does not deliver. It reads 'everything you have extracted, minus everything you carried in', and the comment in addProgress says 'Everything extracted minus everything carried in'. I found no comment or ruling that leaves stall money out on purpose. runEarnings dates from v10.27, which is later than v7.62, where stall money became carried money. The stall already takes part in this bookkeeping: since v13.91, buying at the stall adds to `G.carriedIn`, and that is subtracted here. So a purchase lowers the figure but a sale never raises it.
Concrete case: carry in $3,000 of kit, sell a backpack that brings $7,150 at the stall, then extract with an empty backpack. The run adds -3,000 to Net lifetime earnings, even though $7,150 was banked.
This is not balance: it changes only a displayed counter and no credits, XP or dials. The existing fixture check on this counter in tools/mkfixture.ps1 never sells anything, so with pedSold at 0 its expected values stay the same. Old log rows without pedSold fall back to 0, so profiles from before the counter still sum as before.
The proposed fix is correct: it counts pedSold only on extraction, which matches pay on walk-out and loss on death or abandon.

confirmed.title: The emote bar stays up over the downed screen, V opens it while downed, and its keys do nothing without a word
confirmed.where: damagePlayer going-down block (~line 13220) and raidKey V toggle (~line 11097)
confirmed.code:
G.mapOpen=false; G.bagOpen=false; G.drag=null;   // v14.07, HUD audit: nothing covers the downed screen
  if(code==='KeyV'&&G&&!G.over&&!G.paused&&!G.trade&&!repeat){
confirmed.steps: Press V to bring up the emote bar, for example while lining up a hail on a hostile pillager at range, and get shot down before picking an emote. The going-down block closes the map and the backpack so that nothing covers the downed screen, but it never clears G.emoteBar. drawHUD draws the bar after the red downed wash, so HAIL, STAND DOWN, POINT and THANKS stay drawn over the bleed-out, with the caption 'weapon down, they will listen'. Pressing 1-4 goes to doEmote, which returns on p.downed with no message. V also opens the bar while he is already down, because the toggle has no downed test, unlike the backpack's v14.57 rule.
confirmed.fix:
G.mapOpen=false; G.bagOpen=false; G.drag=null; G.emoteBar=false;   // v14.07, HUD audit: nothing covers the downed screen
  if(code==='KeyV'&&G&&!G.over&&!G.paused&&!G.trade&&!repeat&&!(G.player&&(G.player.downed||G.player.dying))){
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, with the player standing, set G.emoteBar=true and G.mapOpen=true. Drive damagePlayer with lethal damage so he goes down, then assert G.emoteBar===false. The current build leaves it true. The control is that G.mapOpen is false on both builds, which proves the going-down branch ran. Second arm: while p.downed, call raidKey('KeyV',false,null) and assert G.emoteBar stays false. The current build sets it true. Control: after selfRevive, with him standing, raidKey('KeyV',false,null) must set G.emoteBar true on both builds.

verdict.reason: Every step checks out in the current code. (1) In damagePlayer's going-down block, the line `G.mapOpen=false; G.bagOpen=false; G.drag=null;   // v14.07, HUD audit: nothing covers the downed screen` closes the map and the backpack but never touches G.emoteBar. A search for emoteBar finds only five places, and none of them clears it on going down: doEmote's `G.emoteBar=false;`, the V/ESC/TAB close inside raidKey, the V toggle, backOut, and the raid init. killPlayer does not clear it either. (2) drawHUD (starts at `function drawHUD(){`) draws the downed wash at `if(p.downed){ ... ctx.fillStyle='rgba(60,8,5,.45)'; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H);`. Much later in the same function, with no early return in between, it draws `if(G.emoteBar&&!G.trade){`, which has no downed test and prints the caption `weaponDown()?'weapon down, they will listen':'lower your weapon first, or it is just noise'` plus the four EMOTES boxes on top of the bleed-out. (3) While the bar is up, raidKey's `if(G&&!G.over&&!G.trade&&G.emoteBar){` block takes the digits and calls doEmote(en-1). doEmote then hits `if(p.downed||p.roll>0) return;` before any say(), so nothing happens and nothing is said, and the digits never reach the belt. (4) The toggle `if(code==='KeyV'&&G&&!G.over&&!G.paused&&!G.trade&&!repeat){ ... G.emoteBar=!G.emoteBar;` has no downed test. The v14.57 backpack rule (`(G.bagOpen||!(G.player&&(G.player.downed||G.player.dying)))`) does have one. No comment or ruling nearby says this is deliberate, no number moves, and no TXSHIP key or player text changes. The proposed fix is correct. Closing still works while down, because the emote-bar block handles V/ESC/TAB with `G.emoteBar=false; return;` before the toggle line runs. A V pressed while down simply falls through to the generic preventDefault list, which already includes 'KeyV'. p.dying exists: killPlayer sets `G.deathBeat=1.5; p.dying=true;`.

confirmed.title: A controller cannot choose a sector: the sector rows are not in the pad's focus list
confirmed.where: padFocusables, about line 11809 (sector rows built by renderSector, about line 34879)
confirmed.steps: Play with only a controller. Walk to the lift and press A (go up). The sector page opens with COLD STORAGE and THE COLD MILE listed; both are offered (beta:1 on both maps). The D-pad and stick only move between DAY, NIGHT, the six weather buttons, ASCEND TO THIS SECTOR and CLOSE. The two sector cards are div.row.sectorpick, which match none of the selectors, so the highlight can never land on them and A can never press them. A pad-only player always ascends to whatever P.mapIx already holds (COLD STORAGE on a new profile). THE COLD MILE is unreachable and the page's main question, Where are you going?, cannot be answered.
confirmed.test: At 1920x1080, inside the closure: P.mapIx=0; renderSector(); openModal('sectormodal'); var md=document.getElementById('sectormodal'), L=padFocusables(md); var rows=L.filter(function(e){return e.classList.contains('sectorpick');}). On v15.72 rows.length is 0; after the fix it is 2. Control on the same list: L.indexOf(document.getElementById('condnight'))>=0 is true on both builds, which shows the list is live and the page is laid out. Drive arm: stub navigator.getGamepads with one connected pad, all buttons up, and poll once. Then padSetFocus(rows[1]) (fixed build) and poll with button 0 down. Expect P.mapIx===1 and the second card to read ASCENDING HERE. On v15.72 the same drive refocuses to list[focusIx] and P.mapIx stays 0. Control drive on both builds: padSetFocus(#condnight) plus the same A poll sets P.cond to 'night', which proves the pad A path works on this page. Restore P.mapIx and P.cond in finally.

verdict.reason: I confirmed every step in the current code. padFocusables (line 11809) builds its list only from `'button,.cell,.vcell,.crow,.invtab,.scard,.vpill,input,select'`. renderSector (line 34879) builds each sector card as `'<div class="row sectorpick" data-map="'+i+'" ...`. That is a plain div with the classes row and sectorpick, and neither is in the list (.crow is a different class). The only way the card sets P.mapIx is the onclick at lines 34890-34895. padMenu (lines 11854-11928) moves only between items on that list and presses A only as PAD.focus.click(), so a controller can never land on or press a sector card. I found no other controller path to the cards. Neither pollPad nor padMenu has sector-specific code, and the only two references to sectorpick in the file are at lines 34879 and 34888. The other ways onto the page lead to the same cards: the lift's go up act (lines 29168-29175) and the map button (line 34789) both call renderSector() and openModal('sectormodal'). Both maps are offered: BETA_ONE_MAP=true (line 5851), and COLD STORAGE (line 5872) and THE COLD MILE (line 6011) both have beta:1. So a controller-only player can pick day, night and weather but not the sector. They always go up to whatever P.mapIx already holds. No comment or ruling says this is deliberate, and it is not balance. The proposed fix is correct and safe. The cards are display:block and visible, pointer-events is not none, and a div is never disabled, so they pass every filter. The .padfocus outline (line 561) works on a div. After A, renderSector rebuilds the cards, and the v14.22 place-keeping code (lines 11882-11885) puts the highlight back on the same spot in the list. No player text or number changes.

confirmed.title: At NIGHT the in-raid sector map header still names a daylight hour (8am, noon, 6pm)
confirmed.steps: On the sector page press NIGHT (the hint reads You go up in the dark), then ascend and open the map with M or D-UP. buildRaid always rolls G.tod with pickTod, even at night, to keep the random-number sequence the same. Every use of that time of day is gated on isDay() (lamp level, the colour tint, the dim, lampBase), so at night it does nothing, but the map header prints it anyway. Three raids in five open a night raid whose map says noon  Clear, 8am  Rainy or 6pm  Foggy. This is the same contradiction as his v3.59 note that golden hour should not happen at night.
confirmed.test: In a live raid at 1920x1080 on the dry fixture, inside the closure: var rec=[], of=ctx.fillText; ctx.fillText=function(s){ rec.push(String(s)); return of.apply(this,arguments); }; try{ P.cond='night'; G.tod=TODS[2]; G.wxNext=null; drawMapOverlay(); } finally{ ctx.fillText=of; P.cond=saved; }. Then var hdr=rec.filter(function(s){ return s.indexOf('  '+wx().name)>0; }). Build the needle as 'no'+'on'. On v15.72 hdr[0] starts with the needle at night. After the fix it starts with 'night'. Control: the same run with P.cond='day' gives a header starting with the needle on both builds, which proves the recorder catches the header line.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. Each step checks out in the current code:
(1) Night can be reached. The lift's E act runs `liftResetDay();` and then `renderSector(); openModal('sectormodal');`. The NIGHT button handler then sets `P.cond=(this.getAttribute('data-cond')==='night')?'night':'day';`, and the hint reads 'You go up in the dark. XP pays ...'. Nothing resets it to day after that.
(2) buildRaid rolls the hour whether it is day or night: `tod:pickTod(WX_ROLL),`. pickTod draws from `TODS=[DAWN, 8am, noon, 6pm, 8pm]`, and nothing in it checks isDay.
(3) The daylight effects are gated: `wx().lights*(isDay()?tod().lights:1)`, `if(isDay()&&TD.add){`, `if(isDay()&&TD.dim){` and lampBase's `if(!d) return 1;`. One small correction: rain alpha (`var _rl=(typeof tod==='function'&&tod())?tod().lights:0;`) and fog damping still read tod() without a gate, so "every use is gated" is not quite true. That does not affect the header.
(4) The map header prints the hour with no gate: `ctx.fillText(tod().name+'  '+wx().name+`. So a night raid that rolls 8am, noon or 6pm shows that hour, which is 3 rolls in 5. DAWN and 8pm also show at night.
No comment or ruling makes this deliberate. `syncCond` already says 'SURFACE: NIGHT', and the run record stores `night:` separately from `tod`. This is text only, so it is not balance, and it is not a TXSHIP sentence.
The proposed fix is right but misses a second place. The in-raid CONDITIONS panel prints the same label with no gate: `rows.push({k:MT.name+'   '+MW.name,v:(wv.length?wv.join(', '):''),`. Both lines should be fixed.
verdict.correctedFix:
Map header (drawMapOverlay):
  ctx.fillText((isDay()?tod().name:'night')+'  '+wx().name+
Conditions HUD panel (same contradiction, var MW=(G.wx||WEATHER[0]), MT=tod() block):
  rows.push({k:(isDay()?MT.name:'night')+'   '+MW.name,v:(wv.length?wv.join(', '):''),

confirmed.title: The sector card's run count stops at the 60-entry run log, so a long career shows too few runs here, or YOU HAVE NEVER RAIDED HERE
confirmed.where: renderSector, about line 34860; commitRun, about line 19632
confirmed.steps: Play past 60 committed raids; he was at 53 or more. commitRun drops the oldest record once the log passes 60, and the sector card counts only what is left in the log. Example: 80 raids on COLD STORAGE shows you: 60 runs here. Example: 20 early raids on THE COLD MILE followed by 60 on COLD STORAGE makes the Mile card say YOU HAVE NEVER RAIDED HERE. The v12.97 note on netEarn already records that the log keeps only the last sixty runs.
confirmed.test: Inside the closure, with a profile snapshot restored through the loader in finally: P.log=[]; for 60 times push {mapName:'COLD STORAGE',outcome:'extract',_committed:1}; commitRun({mapName:'COLD STORAGE',outcome:'extract',haul:0,containers:0,dist:0}); renderSector(); read document.querySelector('#sectorlist .sectorpick[data-map="0"]').textContent. On v15.72 it contains you: 60 runs here; after the fix it contains you: 61 runs here. Control: seed 10 records instead of 60 and the text reads you: 11 runs here on both builds, which proves the counting and the render path work below the cap.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. Every step checks out in the current code.

1. commitRun, around line 19628: `P.log.push(rec);` is followed by `if(P.log.length>60) P.log.shift();`. The oldest record is thrown away for good.
2. renderSector, around line 34860: the card counts only what is left in the log (`for(var _mr=0;_mr<P.log.length;_mr++) if(P.log[_mr].mapName===M.name) _myR++;`). It then prints `'you: '+_myR+' run'+...+' here'`, or 'YOU HAVE NEVER RAIDED HERE' when the count is 0.
3. Every committed run has a map name: the record sets `mapName:FIXED_MAPS[clamp(...)].name`. Bot-sim runs never reach commitRun (`if(!G.sim) commitRun(pendingRun);`), so they cannot skew the count.
4. The v12.97 note in restoreMake says the log keeps only the last sixty runs. P.runs and P.netEarn are kept as separate lifetime counters for exactly that reason, but nothing keeps a lifetime count per map.
5. Nothing marks the undercount as deliberate. It is a wrong fact on the card, not balance, and the wording does not change, so no TXSHIP key is affected.
6. So 80 raids on COLD STORAGE shows 60, and a map whose raids have all aged out of the log reads YOU HAVE NEVER RAIDED HERE.
7. The 'Clear recorder' button (`P.log=[]`) causes the same false 'never raided' message for every map. The new counter fixes that too, because Clear recorder does not touch it.

The proposed fix is correct as far as it goes:
- saveProfile writes the whole P with JSON.stringify(P), so P.mapRunN is saved and loaded.
- The name mapRunN is not used anywhere else.
- It is seeded from the log once, so an old save keeps whatever its log still holds.

It misses one case: restoreApply resets per-character state (`P.seals={}; P.mapSeen={};`) and does not touch the log. If nothing else changes, a restored character would carry the replaced character's lifetime per-map counts. That is the mistake v15.00 to v15.02 fixed for rivals and contracts. The corrected fix below carries the counter in the restore code as well.

confirmed.title: A hired pillager on FOLLOW walks toward a cache behind a still-locked door, then stands against the wall and stops following
confirmed.where: updateEnts, merc FOLLOW branch, about line 18791 (the pick loop under 'v15.19, hire audit finding: AND HE DOES NOT PICK A CRATE YOU STARTED')
confirmed.steps: No container ever has .locked (or .mine) set. Grep shows the only containers inside a room are tagged inLocked (line 10066), the strongbox is placed there by spotIn, and ordinary crates can land there too. So the filter lets through the three caches in each locked room. Steps: hire a pillager (FOLLOW is the default order). On COLD STORAGE, walk past the south side of BLAST FREEZER or FOREMAN OFFICE, or stand at its door prompt, key or no key. Once he is within 160 of a cache inside, he picks it. navPath gives no route because the goal is in another region, so seekPoint steers him straight at it and he grinds along the room's shell wall. He never gets within 30 of it. The pick is only dropped when he is 280 from the box, which the 220 to 240 rooms never allow, or when you get 420 from him. So he stays put and stops following for as long as you stay nearby. When you spend the key he is already aimed at the cache, walks in, and takes the vault cache into his pack before you reach it.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. Every step checks out in the current code.

1. The `locked` test in the pick filter never fires. The filter is `if(_CT.opened||_CT.locked||_CT.mine||(_CT.prog||0)>0) continue;`, but nothing in the file ever sets `.locked` on a container. `mkContainer` returns `{x,y,r,type,d,loot,opened,time,best,rot,pulled}` with no `locked` field. The only matches for `.locked` are that filter line and `map.locked` room lists. Nothing ever sets `.mine` on a container either. So the filter only really checks `opened` and `prog`.

2. Caches inside a locked room are marked a different way. The room placer runs `lcc.cache=1; lcc.inLocked=LR.id;`, three per room. The strongbox is dropped into a random locked room by `spotIn`. The reach pass leaves ordinary crates inside locked rooms on purpose (its comment: "Sitting INSIDE a locked room counts as by design even without the flag"). All of these pass the pick filter.

3. The pick itself is `if(dist(e,_CT)<160&&dist(p,_CT)<420){ e.mgoal=_CT; ...}`. On COLD STORAGE, BLAST FREEZER and FOREMAN OFFICE are both 230x230. Their caches sit inside the room at `{x+20,y+20,w-40,h-40}`, so a hire standing outside the south wall or at the door is well within 160 of one.

4. He cannot get there. `navSeek` asks `navPath`, which returns null when `nav.region[start]!==nav.region[goal]`. Its own v3.71 comment names this exact case: "a raider asking for a route to a cache inside a still-locked room". With no route, `seekPoint` walks him straight at the cache, then hugs the wall. The hug only lets go when the way ahead is clear and he is closer, which never happens here.

5. Nothing drops the pick in time. The drop line is `if(e.mgoal&&(e.mgoal.opened||(e.mgoal.prog||0)>0||dist(e,e.mgoal)>280))`. He only needs to be within 30 of the cache to loot it, and the outer `if(dF<420&&!p.downed)` clears the goal only once you are 420 from him. While `e.mgoal` is set, the `else` that follows you (`if(dF>120) navSeek(e,p.x,p.y,...)`) never runs. So he stops following while you stay within 420.

6. When the key is spent, `doorNear.open=true`, the door wall is removed and `rebuildGeometry()` runs. He is still aimed at the cache, gets a route, and loots it: `e.bag.push(e.mgoal.loot[_mq])`.

Nothing marks this as deliberate. The v15.19 comments above the filter are about crates you have started searching. Doors cannot be destroyed (`if(w.noDes||w.lockWall||w.door||w.ledge) return null;`), and the only place that sets `.open` on a room is the key spend. So a room's `open` flag is the right thing to test.

The proposed fix is correct as written:
- The room objects carry `{x,y,w,h,open}`.
- The strict inside test matches the one the reach pass already uses: `RC.x>LQ.x&&RC.x<LQ.x+LQ.w&&...`.
- It covers caches, the strongbox and stray crates alike.
- Once a door opens, those boxes become legal again.
- A room never closes again, so the drop line does not need changing.
- The name `shutRoomAt` is not used anywhere else. The only `inLocked` function is a local inside the nav builder, not a global.
- No text, number or random draw changes, so this is a bug fix, not balance.

verdict.reason:
I couldn't refute it. The trap is real, but one step and one word in the claim are wrong.

1. The spot test only looks at walls. freeSpot rejects a point only when it is within pad of a wall rect: `if(x>w.x-pad&&x<w.x+w.w+pad&&y>w.y-pad&&y<w.y+w.h+pad){ok=0;break;}`. A locked room is five 16-unit strips plus a door strip (`walls.push({x:LK.x,y:LK.y,w:LK.w,h:lt,d:3,lockWall:LK.id});` and the others, lt=16). With pad 30, a 230 room leaves open interior from 46 to 184 on each axis, so about 138 by 138, as claimed. COLD STORAGE is w:4200 h:3400 with `{id:'cs_office',  name:'FOREMAN OFFICE',  x:3820,y:250,  w:230,h:230}` in the NE corner.
2. Nothing checks a pillager's spot after placement.
   - The opening roster does `var s3=far(freeSpot(map,30),1190);` and then `var R3=mkRaider(s3.x,s3.y,_ident,sim);` with no check between.
   - _capHouses only moves crawlers (`if(!_E3||_E3.kind!=='crawler') continue;`).
   - The v2.12 reach pass under `if(CFG.cacheReach!==0){` only walks `containers`.
   - mkRaider has no position fix-up.
   - Waves take the farthest of 24 with `if(_cd>bd){ bd=_cd; sp=_c; }` and only check `if(!sp||bd<900) return;`.
3. He loots the room. mkRaider starts him in `state:'loot'`. The loot branch picks the nearest unopened container, and the only filters are `if(ct.opened) continue;` and skips. Nothing skips `inLocked` caches or the strongbox. Inside the room, walkClearR/navSeek reach the caches, and the pull runs `e.goal.opened=true; for(...) e.bag.push(e.goal.loot[q]);`.
4. The map shows it. The sector map draws `mapLabel(CQ.opened?'LOOTED':'CACHE',...)` for every `CQ.cache`, so the room's caches read LOOTED before the player finds the key.
5. He cannot leave. The walls hold until `doorNear.open=true` and the door wall is spliced. The only stuck watchdog (`e._stuckT`) belongs to the Peddler.

What is wrong in the claim:
- He does not switch to extract after the caches. CFG has raiderHaul:7, and the room holds 3 caches, plus the strongbox and the odd crate at most. So he stays in 'loot' and drops each outside container after about 3 seconds each (`if(e.pathFail||...) e.skips.push(e.goal)`). He is still trapped until the door opens, so the outcome stands.
- "Likely" is too strong. My rough estimate is a few percent per wave with the player in the SW, and about 0.5 percent per opening raider per room.

This is a placement bug, not balance, and no ruling or comment makes it deliberate.

The proposed fix does not work as written: shutRoomAt does not exist anywhere in the file (grep finds no match). The fix needs the helper defined, and it should skip rooms already opened.
